Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: "Tales from Ovid" by Ted Hughes: Read-Aloud and Discussion of an Often Banned Poet NEW — Sat Oct 10, 11:00 AM — Montclair Main - Tower Room
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
The Roman poet Ovid has been upsetting censors for more than two thousand years. The emperor Augustus exiled Ovid from Rome shortly after the publication of his Metamorphoses. All Ovid's works were burned by Savonarola in the infamous "bonfire of the vanities" in 1497. And when Shakespeare's rival Christopher Marlowe translated Ovid a century later, the translation was set on fire again in the "Bishop's Ban." Then the U.S. Customs censored some of Ovid's work again in 1930.
To celebrate Banned Books Week, we'll be reading aloud and discussing "Tales from Ovid: 24 Passages from the Metamorphoses," an award-winning retelling by the longtime British poet laureate Ted Hughes. Come to class and hear for yourself what all fuss is about!
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Tuesday Open Studio Figure Drawing — Tue Oct 13, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Every Tuesday, 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space | All skill levels welcome *Cover art by Ling Chen.
Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. Each week a different model – usually nude, and sometimes clothed – serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say, observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a supportive community of seekers, artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Oct 14, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: The Winding History of School Sports: A Unique American Invention NEW — Wed Oct 14, 2:00 PM — Montclair - Offsite
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class taking place at the Yogi Berra Museum. Click here to register.
Why do American schools build stadiums, award athletic scholarships, pay coaches extravagant salaries even as academic programs get cut, and turn teenagers into campus heroes - while most of the world keeps sports completely separate from education? This lively talk explores the surprising history behind the uniquely American idea of the "student-athlete". By comparing the US system with the European model of independent sports clubs, we'll uncover how this unusual partnership began, why it became so powerful, and what it means for education - and the futures - of young athletes today.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: From Swastika to Jim Crow (2000): Screening and Discussion NEW — Sun Oct 25, 2:00 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
This is a free Adult School class. Registration is required
Explore an influential, little-known chapter in the history of Black-Jewish relations in America. We'll be screening a documentary film, From Swastika to Jim Crow, based on a book by the same title by Gabrielle Simon Edgcomb. It tells the story of German-Jewish refugees, who, expelled from their homeland by Hitler and the Nazis, found new lives and careers at historically Black colleges and universities in the American South, influencing a whole generation of Black students and professionals. After the screening, Dr. Lillie Johnson Edwards and Rabbi Julie Roth, will discuss the film's significance. Dr. Edwards is a Drew University Professor Emerita of History and African American Studies. Rabbi Roth leads Congregation Shomrei Emunah of Montclair, NJ.
This program is co-sponsored by Shomrei Emunah (https://shomrei.org/) and The Mark Montclair https://themarkmtc.org).
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306
